claims.description: Dry-run derives the current envelope matrix demand, checked-in baseline sum, and 10% headroom without truncation.

Runner tests prove per-flow attempted, completed, budget-skipped, and required-sample accounting, including a flow that reports incomplete because a pre-call skip drops attempted below required with zero budget-skips.

Gate tests prove zero/partial exhaustion fails closed while incomplete coverage is excluded from BaselineDrift, an incomplete flow absent from baseline.json still fails the coverage gate, and --update-baseline refuses to accept (gate) or write (index.ts seed-guard) incomplete coverage.
Index summary code prints configured versus required demand and per-flow coverage.

Pure mastery budget tests cover the complete grid, changed counts, 215 rejection, 216 acceptance, and derive that 216 configured versus 192 expected leaves exactly three 8-call reproduce rounds for one offender.

Workflow comments record matrix-derived envelope provider demand including internal judge calls, sequential estimated provider demand, and gate-specific caps. Timeout re-verification: the comment projects each gate's retained-run-30721918215 wall clock (envelope 839s, teaching 271s, mastery 710s) onto CURRENT demand via ratios grounded in that run's own log (envelope 366/300, teaching 5/5, mastery 24/21) to ~35.1 min / ~5.1x headroom under the unchanged 180-minute timeout-minutes, with explicit uncertainty (single run, no P90, 2 failed envelope OUTER invocations, queue/latency variance, and now an honest disclosure that 29 of that run's 33 skips were budget-exceeded - 16 judge-bearing safety-probes/language-quality cases and 13 other non-judge-bearing cases, not all 29 judge-bearing). No paid live run performed; timeout-minutes itself unchanged. Review-fix round 1 (adversarial review on PR #2909, M1+S1): (M1) the deterministic test's headroom computation and its assertion on the comment's stated timeout now both read timeout-minutes from the parsed workflow YAML (loadJobTimeoutMinutes) instead of a hardcoded 180 literal, proven by a temporary timeout-minutes:180->20 mutation (RED) that was then reverted byte-identically (GREEN); (S1) the comment's 300 denominator is now labeled explicitly as the retained run's outer-runLive()-invocation cap (not a measured provider-call count), and 366/300 is described as a conservative scaling comparison, not like-for-like measured throughput; the teaching term is a ratio (271s x 5/5) bound to current TEACHING_SCENARIOS.length. Review-fix round 2 (0 MUST_FIX/2 SHOULD_FIX/3 CONSIDER): (SHOULD-1) the test's three ratio checks were loose toContain substring matches vulnerable to superset false-positives (366/300 inside 366/3000) and incidental matches (5/5); replaced with numBoundary-guarded regexes binding each full 'duration x ratio' expression, proven by a 366/300->366/3000 mutation RED then byte-identical revert GREEN; (SHOULD-2) added the 29/33-skip disclosure above to the workflow comment, independently re-derived from the retained run log; (CONSIDER) the timeout-minutes regex gained the same numBoundary guard so a mutated 2-digit value cannot match as a substring of the real 3-digit 180 - per explicit instruction, no expect(timeout).toBe(180) assertion was added.
Deterministic workflow-contract tests pin derived provider-demand relationships, omitted-cap preflight ordering, runtime order, and changed counts without a fixed envelope-only assertion.
